extracted.intended_audience: Early-career UK-based scientists (or researchers returning from a career break) preparing applications to the Royal Society Research Grants scheme
extracted.subtask_description: Preparing and submitting an application for the Royal Society Research Grants scheme (seed-corn funding up to £30,000 for up to 12 months) targeted at newly independent researchers or those returning from a career break. Includes eligibility, required application components, permitted costs, and the panel assessment process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility — doctoral qualification
rubrics_metrics.description: You hold a PhD or equivalent qualification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Read the scheme notes for further information on eligibility. Ensure you meet all eligibility requirements before applying.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility — early independent research stage (first five years)
rubrics_metrics.description: You are within the first five years of an independent research post at the time of application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This can be either your first permanent independent academic research post, your first independent research fellowship or a named limited-tenured/fixed-term academic research post, obtained in open competition. Note that tenure must cover the duration of the award. A table of example eligible career positions is provided in Annex 1 of the scheme notes to help assess eligibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility — returning from a career break
rubrics_metrics.description: The scheme is also for independent researchers returning to academia after a career break to enable them to develop new ideas and research questions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Annex 1 and scheme notes for examples and further guidance on how career-break returners fit eligibility criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility — institutional and residency requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: You are based at an eligible UK organisation and a UK resident at the time of application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confirm your host organisation is eligible (see scheme notes and the Royal Society pages).

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility — demonstrable independence
rubrics_metrics.description: You are a fully independent researcher with access to your own lab space and with the ability to recruit and be registered as the primary supervisor of PhD students and research assistants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant must show they have their own independent research environment and supervisory responsibilities appropriate to an independent researcher.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project remit — Royal Society natural sciences scope
rubrics_metrics.description: Your research is within the Royal Society’s remit of natural sciences (includes, but not limited to, biological research and biomedical sciences, chemistry, engineering, mathematics and physics).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For a full list, consult the breakdown of subject groups and areas supported by the Royal Society linked on the scheme page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding amount and duration limits
rubrics_metrics.description: The scheme provides up to £30,000 of funding for up to 12 months.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan your project, budget and timeline to fit within the £30,000 and 12-month maximum; full funding details and permitted/forbidden costs are set out in the scheme notes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permitted costs / allowable uses of funds
rubrics_metrics.description: Funds can cover equipment; consumables; travel costs and subsistence for essential field research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult the scheme notes for full funding details and any cost justification expectations. The scheme is described as providing ‘seed corn’ funding specifically to purchase specialised equipment and consumables.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project purpose alignment (scheme objectives)
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposals should enable newly independent researchers to gather preliminary data, develop their research ideas and strengthen applications for further funding; support returners from career breaks to develop new ideas; and increase availability of equipment and consumables for early-career researchers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications should be written and scoped to meet these objectives; updated guidance to support writing the research proposal is included in the scheme notes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required application components
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must submit a research proposal, a lay summary, and (new for this round) a scientific abstract; applicants must also identify the primary subject area of the research proposal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Updated guidance on writing the research proposal is included in the scheme notes. The application form contains a new question to identify the primary subject area. Follow the word/section limits and formatting guidance in the scheme notes and Flexi-Grant system.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application submission platform and process
rubrics_metrics.description: You will apply through the Royal Society’s application and grant management system, Flexi-Grant®.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See the 'Application and assessment process' page for a general overview and the scheme notes for full details. Ensure you follow deadlines and submission requirements (open date and close date listed on the page).

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment process and review mechanics
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment is overseen by the Royal Society Research Grants panel: following eligibility checks, applications are initially reviewed and assessed by a minimum of two panel members with the most appropriate scientific expertise; shortlisted applications are reviewed by the Panel Chair and recommendations for funding are made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect multidisciplinary expert review; ensure your proposal is clear to expert reviewers. Full details of the review process and selection steps are in the scheme notes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equity, diversity and inclusion in assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: The Society embeds EDI principles in grant making to ensure all talented applicants have an equitable chance to succeed as per assessment criteria.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policies and processes are regularly reviewed and revised to embed EDI. Applicants should note EDI commitments and may find further guidance in scheme notes or Royal Society policy pages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support and adjustments for disabled applicants
rubrics_metrics.description: The Royal Society provides adjustments to ensure disabled applicants can participate fully (examples include extension of the deadline; additional support to complete the application form; receiving the application form in a different format such as Word; support during interviews including technical support for accessibility software; additional costs incurred to attend an interview).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests for adjustments are treated confidentially and will not normally be shared with panel members unless relevant to assessment; contact researchgrants@royalsociety.org or the Grants Team for confidential support. Any sharing of adjustment details will be done with the applicant's permission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Condition — tenure/contract must cover award duration
rubrics_metrics.description: If your independent post is a limited-tenured/fixed-term academic research post, the tenure/contract must cover the duration of the award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confirm employment/contract dates and provide evidence if required during eligibility checks; see scheme notes for details on documentation.
